newsitem.title: TURKEY: Perry leaves Turkey after Iraq talks.
newsitem.headline: Perry leaves Turkey after Iraq talks.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry left Ankara on Monday after brief talks with Turkish leaders on Washington's efforts to maintain military and economic pressure against neighbouring Iraq.

"They were good consultations," Perry told reporters at Ankara airport, before boarding a U.S. air force C-17 transport plane. He took no questions but aides said a written statement was expected later in the day.
Earlier Perry met Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller for a working breakfast and held talks with the army chief of staff and President Suleyman Demirel.
The visit to Turkey was part of a broader diplomatic offensive that took Perry to Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Bahrain.

Turkey hosts Operation Provide Comfort, the U.S.-led air force patrolling northern Iraq, but has grown increasingly impatient with a mission critics say fosters Kurdish separatism and impinges on Turkish sovereignty.
Ankara is keen to normalise ties with Iraq, its third biggest trading partner until U.N. sanctions were slapped on Baghdad for its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
